title: Why Were There Giants After the Flood?
paragraphs:
Why Were There Giants After the Flood?
The Mystery That Shakes Genesis, Challenges Traditions, and Reveals a Greater Story of Grace
Most people never notice it.
They read Genesis, see the Flood destroy the world, and assume every trace of the ancient corruption disappeared beneath the waters.
Then they keep reading.
And suddenly, centuries later, giants are standing in the Promised Land.
The question hits like thunder.
If the Flood destroyed everything outside Noah's Ark, why were there giants after the Flood?
How did they survive?
Did some of the Nephilim board the Ark?
Was the Flood incomplete?
Or is there something deeper happening in Scripture that many believers have overlooked?
What if the answer is not merely about giants?
What if it is about the relentless war between corruption and redemption...
and the even greater truth that no scandal, no rebellion, and no darkness can stop God's plan to bring salvation through Jesus Christ?
The story begins in one of the most mysterious passages in the entire Bible.
Genesis 6:1-4 says:
"When man began to multiply on the face of the land and daughters were born to them, the sons of God saw that the daughters of man were attractive. And they took as their wives any they chose."
Then Scripture declares:
"The Nephilim were on the earth in those days—and also afterward..."
That final phrase is impossible to ignore.
"And also afterward."
In Hebrew, the text reads:

"וְגַם אַחֲרֵי־כֵן"
(vegam acharei-ken)
"And also after that."
The Bible itself anticipates the question.
The Nephilim existed before the Flood...
and somehow there were giant clans after it.
The Hebrew word translated "Nephilim" is:

נְפִלִים
(Nephilim)
Its exact meaning is debated, but it is often connected to the root נפל (naphal), meaning "to fall."
Many scholars understand Nephilim as "fallen ones."
Others understand them as mighty warriors or tyrannical giants.
Whatever interpretation one adopts, Scripture presents them as extraordinary figures connected with widespread corruption before the Flood.
The Bible does not provide every detail modern readers wish it did.
That can be frustrating.
But God did not write Scripture to satisfy every curiosity.
He wrote it to reveal Himself.
And that changes everything.
The first theory people often hear is that some Nephilim somehow survived the Flood physically.
Yet Scripture repeatedly emphasizes the total destruction of the pre-Flood world.
Genesis 7:23 states:
"Every living thing that was on the face of the ground was wiped out."
The language leaves little room for secret survivors.
The biblical record consistently teaches that only Noah, his family, and the animals preserved on the Ark survived.
That is why many biblical scholars reject the idea that pre-Flood Nephilim physically survived.
A second explanation is that similar events occurred again after the Flood.
Those who hold the supernatural interpretation of Genesis 6 suggest that whatever produced the Nephilim before the Flood happened again later.
This view attempts to explain why giant clans appear centuries afterward.
Groups such as the Anakim, Rephaim, Emim, and Zamzummim are described as unusually large people.
Numbers 13:33 records the fearful report of Israel's spies:
"We seemed to ourselves like grasshoppers."
The Anakim appeared terrifying.
Massive.
Overwhelming.
Impossible to defeat.
Yet notice something important.
The Bible never directly calls the Anakim descendants of pre-Flood Nephilim.
The frightened spies make that connection.
Whether their assessment was completely accurate is another question entirely.

A third explanation, held by many conservative scholars, is that the word Nephilim became a broader term for powerful warriors or giant peoples rather than referring exclusively to the beings of Genesis 6.
In this view, later giants were not survivors of the original Nephilim but distinct groups whose great size reminded people of those ancient legends.
The truth is that Scripture does not settle every detail beyond dispute.
And perhaps that is intentional.
Because when we become obsessed with giants, we can miss the greater story standing directly in front of us.
The giants are not the heroes.
The giants are not even the point.
God is.
Think about it.
Humanity rebelled.
Violence filled the earth.
Genesis says the thoughts of people's hearts were continually evil.
The Hebrew phrase is devastating:

"רַק רַע כָּל־הַיּוֹם"
(raq ra kol hayom)
"Only evil all the day."
The Flood was not merely judgment.
It was a response to a world consumed by corruption.
Yet even there, grace appears.
Genesis 6:8 says:
"But Noah found favor in the eyes of the LORD."
The Hebrew word translated favor is:

חֵן
(chen)
Grace.
Unmerited favor.
Noah's story was never ultimately about a boat.
It was about grace.
And that pattern continues throughout Scripture.
Giants appear.
Empires rise.
Sin spreads.
Human beings fail repeatedly.
Yet God keeps writing a different ending.
When Israel encountered giants in Canaan, fear spread through the camp.
Everyone saw the size of the enemy.
Few remembered the size of God.
Then a shepherd boy named David walked onto a battlefield.
The giant towered above him.
Experienced.
Armored.
Terrifying.
But David understood something Goliath did not.
Victory never belonged to the strongest man.
Victory belonged to God.
The giant fell.
Not because David was extraordinary.
But because the Lord was faithful.
The same pattern reaches its climax at the Cross.
Humanity's greatest giant was never Goliath.
It was sin.
The giant was guilt.
The giant was death.
The giant was separation from God.
Every human being eventually stands before those giants.
Some hide behind success.
Others hide behind religion.
Others bury themselves in distractions.
Yet the giants remain.
Fear.
Shame.
Regret.
Addiction.
Failure.
Broken relationships.
Secret sins.
Scandals nobody else sees.
And that is why the Gospel is such astonishing news.
Jesus Christ stepped into humanity's battlefield and confronted the giant none of us could defeat.
At the Cross He carried our sin.
At the empty tomb He conquered death.
What looked like scandal became salvation.
What looked like defeat became victory.
What looked like the end became a new beginning.
That is the heartbeat of Scripture.
Not giants.
Grace.
Not fear.
Redemption.
Not darkness.
Christ.
The New Testament captures this beautifully.
When Jesus cried from the Cross:

Τετέλεσται
(Tetelestai)
"It is finished."
He declared that the debt of sin had been paid in full.
The greatest enemy had been defeated.
The greatest giant had fallen.
And because of that, your story does not have to end where your failures began.
Maybe you came here curious about ancient giants.
But perhaps the real giant standing before you today is something else.
A past you cannot escape.
A mistake you cannot undo.
A shame you cannot silence.
A wound you cannot heal.
The Gospel declares that Jesus Christ still rewrites stories.
He is still turning scandals into testimonies.
Still turning rebels into sons and daughters.
Still turning broken people into new creations.
That is why our mission exists.
Not merely to answer difficult Bible questions.
But to help people encounter the Savior who stands behind every page of Scripture.
What giant has God helped you overcome?
Your testimony may encourage someone who is struggling in silence right now.
They are helping spread the Gospel.
They are helping place biblical truth into more homes, more devices, more hearts, and more lives.
Because one day, nobody will remember how large the giants were.
But eternity will remember what Jesus Christ did with the people who trusted Him.
The giant is never the final chapter when Christ is holding the pen.
